image_description: A close-up, high-resolution portrait of a male mallard duck (drake) resting with its head tucked back onto its shoulder. The image highlights the iridescent green head, yellow bill with a black tip, and the transition from the brown chest to the grey/white body feathers. The background is a smooth, out-of-focus grey-blue.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green with a distinct black tip (nail), matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although only part of the body is visible, the feather density and texture appear realistic and waterproof. The curvature suggests a stocky, compact form.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shows strong iridescent green coloration. The chest is reddish-brown (chestnut) transitioning to lighter feathers, which is characteristic of a male mallard in breeding plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely occluded by the body and the angle of the shot; they are not visible in the frame.
The wings are folded against the body and largely obscured by the head and neck position; their full shape cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the frame or completely occluded by the body angle.
